tip: One word. Stress the end.

lesson.background: The first thing you say when you walk in, until late morning. Fine with hosts and older family.
facts: One word. The stress is at the end.
It is polite on its own. You do not add a name.

tip: Jeni is the polite you. Use this with parents-in-law.

lesson.background: Right after hello, with someone older, a host, or more than one person.
facts: Si means how.
Jeni is you, polite or plural. With one friend your age it is Si je?
If they are tired, a man says i lodhur. A woman says e lodhur.

tip: Faleminderit is the full thank-you. People often shorten the sound in real talk.

lesson.background: Your usual answer when someone asks how you are.
facts: Jam means I am. Mirë is well.
Faleminderit is thank you. In fast talk the middle gets shorter.

tip: Ju lutem is please. Flisni is the polite speak.

lesson.background: When they talk too fast. You can say it in the middle of the conversation.
facts: Ju lutem is please.
Flisni is speak, for polite you or for more than one person.
Ngadalë is slowly.

tip: Nuk is the not. Say it plainly.

lesson.background: When the words went past you. Say it plainly, then ask them to repeat.
facts: Nuk is not.
Kuptoj is I understand. Together: I don't understand.

tip: Përsërisni is the polite repeat.

lesson.background: When you heard the sound but not the words. They will say the same line again.
facts: Përsërisni is repeat, polite you.
The words they repeat are not a set phrase. They say the line again, more slowly.

tip: Point at the thing when you say kjo.

lesson.background: Point at the thing, then ask. They answer with the word for it.
facts: Si thuhet is how is it said.
Kjo is this, for a feminine thing. Ky is this for a masculine thing.
Coffee below is only an example. They name whatever you point at.

tip: A turns it into a yes-or-no question. Doni is polite you want.

lesson.background: You are offering coffee, at home or when you are helping the host.
facts: A doni is do you want, polite.
Kafe is coffee.

tip: Q sounds like the ch in cheap.

lesson.background: The usual order when you want milk in it.
facts: Me is with. Qumësht is milk.
Ju lutem at the end is please.

tip: Say it as you gesture to a chair.

lesson.background: Say it as you gesture to a chair. You are the one offering the seat.
facts: Uluni is sit down, polite.
A family member talking to one person may say ulu instead. This course stays with ju.

tip: Same start as the coffee question. Swap the thing.

lesson.background: Same question shape as coffee. You are offering bread.
facts: Bukë is bread. Swap the thing, keep A doni.

tip: Ë is a soft uh, like the a in sofa.

lesson.background: At the table, about the food in front of you. Kjo is this dish.
facts: Ë is a soft uh, like the a in sofa.
E mirë is good, feminine, matching kjo.

tip: Useful when someone keeps offering food. Some speakers add i (men) or e (women) before ngopur.

lesson.background: When someone keeps offering food. Kind, and clear.
facts: Ngopur is full.
Some speakers add i before it for a man, or e for a woman. This line has neither. It is still used.

tip: A warm line at the end of a visit.

lesson.background: A warm line at the end of a visit, not for a single cup of coffee.
facts: Për is for. Gjithçka is everything.

tip: Ju keeps it polite for parents-in-law. Duam is we love.

lesson.background: For parents-in-law and older family. Ju keeps it polite.
facts: Duam is we love.
Shumë is a lot.
To one person your own age, people say të duam. This course stays with ju.

english: It is good that I am with you.
albanian: Është mirë të jem me ju.
phonetic: UHSH-tuh MEER tuh yem meh yoo
tip: Jem is I am. Me ju is with you, polite.

lesson.background: Sometime in the visit, not only at the door.
facts: Të jem is to be, I.
Me ju is with you, polite.

tip: Softer than Si jeni. This one is about the body.

lesson.background: Softer than Si jeni. This one is about the body.
facts: Ndiheni is you feel, polite.
Use it when someone looks tired or unwell, not every hello.

tip: This is the masculine form. A woman says e lodhur instead of i lodhur.

lesson.background: You are a bit tired, not sick.
facts: This is the masculine form. A woman says e lodhur instead of i lodhur.
Pak keeps it small. Without pak it sounds stronger.

tip: Dh is one sound, like the th in this.

lesson.background: You are asking them. Dh is one sound, like the th in this.
facts: A ju dhemb is does it hurt you.
Diçka is something.

tip: Ç sounds like the ch in church.

lesson.background: A real question for the day, after hello. Polite you.
facts: Çfarë is what. Po bëni is are you doing. Sot is today.
Ç sounds like the ch in church.

reply.english: Do you want to take a walk?

english: Do you want to take a walk?
tip: Shëtisim is we walk, as in shall we stroll.

lesson.background: An invitation to stroll. Shëtisim is we walk.
facts: A doni të is would you like to.
They can say yes, no, or later.

tip: A simple goodbye when you will see them the next day.

lesson.background: A simple goodbye when you will see them the next day.
facts: Shihemi is we'll see each other. Nesër is tomorrow.

tip: Same start, swap the verb: pi (drink), pushoj (rest), shkoj (go).

lesson.background: I want to eat. The start stays. You swap the verb.
facts: Dua të is I want to.
Ha is eat. Pi is drink. Pushoj is rest. Shkoj is go.
Those swaps are the next lines.

tip: Same start, swap the verb: hani (eat), pini (drink). Uleni is sit down, polite.

lesson.background: Do you want to sit.
facts: A doni të is do you want to, polite.
Uleni is sit down, for ju.

tip: Mund të is can I. Offer this at the table.

lesson.background: Can I help. Offer this at the table or in the kitchen.
facts: Mund të is can I.
Ndihmoj is I help.

tip: Safe from late morning through the afternoon.

lesson.background: From late morning through the afternoon. Safe with anyone.
facts: One word, same shape as good morning.
The stress is on di.

tip: From early evening.

lesson.background: From early evening, when you arrive for dinner.
facts: One word. Same pattern as good morning.
Not the word you use when you leave.

tip: When leaving, not when you arrive.

lesson.background: When you are leaving for the night, not when you arrive.
facts: Natën is the night. E mirë is good.
Say it at the door.

tip: Neutral, any time of day.

lesson.background: Any time of day, when a morning or evening word does not fit.
facts: Neutral and polite.
A bit more formal than a quick hello.

tip: A traditional hello. It lands well with elders.

lesson.background: A traditional hello. It lands well with older people.
facts: Longer than a casual hello.
Use it once, at the start.

tip: The standard goodbye.

lesson.background: The full goodbye, when you are actually leaving.
facts: One word.
Clear and polite. Use the shorter one if you will see them again soon.

tip: Lighter than a full goodbye.

lesson.background: Lighter than a full goodbye. You expect to see them again soon.
facts: Shihemi means we will see each other.
Më vonë means later.

tip: After you say you are well. Polite you.

lesson.background: After you have said you are well. It turns the question back, politely.
facts: Po here means and. Ju is polite you.
With one friend your age it is Po ti?

tip: Polite. With a friend people say Si quhesh?

lesson.background: When you are introduced and you do not know their name yet. Polite.
facts: Quheni is polite you are called. With one friend it is Si quhesh?
Wikivoyage prints the informal Si e ke emrin? This card stays polite.
Ana is only an example. The name goes right after quhem.

tip: Say your name right after it.

lesson.background: Right after they ask your name. Say your own name immediately after this.
facts: Unë is I. Quhem is I am called.
Nothing goes between quhem and your name.

tip: Short. Smile and use it once.

lesson.background: Once, after the names. Then move on. Do not repeat it all evening.
facts: Short. It also means I am glad.
If they say it first, Edhe mua means me too.

tip: The one word to use constantly.

lesson.background: The word you will use most. After food, help, a seat, a kindness.
facts: One word. Start with the full word.
In fast speech the middle gets shorter.

tip: When the kindness was bigger.

lesson.background: When the kindness was bigger than a small favor.
facts: Shumë means very, or a lot.
It comes after faleminderit.

tip: The usual answer to thank you.

lesson.background: When someone thanks you. This is the usual answer.
facts: It means there is no reason to thank me.
Ju lutem also works as you're welcome.

tip: Say it. A nod is easy to miss.

lesson.background: A clear yes. A nod is easy to miss across a table.
facts: Po is yes.
The same word means and in Po ju? The tone is different.

tip: Sounds like yo, not joe.

lesson.background: A clear no. If you are refusing food or a favor, add please.
facts: Jo sounds like yo, not joe.
A softer no is Jo, ju lutem.

tip: Also works as you're welcome.

lesson.background: Before a request, and also as a soft you're welcome.
facts: Ju is polite you. Lutem is please.
With one friend it is Të lutem.

tip: To get attention, or to say sorry.

lesson.background: To get someone's attention, or as a small sorry. Then say what you need.
facts: Më falni is excuse me, polite.
Wikivoyage uses this same line, both to get attention and to beg pardon.

tip: When something actually went wrong.

lesson.background: When something actually went wrong. Heavier than excuse me.
facts: Më vjen keq is I'm sorry, literally it comes badly to me.
Save më falni for a bump or a small interruption.

tip: Polite you. Ask this before you give up.

lesson.background: Ask this before you switch languages. Many people will meet you halfway.
facts: A turns it into a yes-or-no question.
Flisni is speak, polite you. Anglisht is English.
Wikivoyage prints this same question.

tip: People warm up when they hear this.

lesson.background: Say this early. People usually slow down and smile.
facts: Flas is I speak.
Pak is a little. Shqip is Albanian.
Wikivoyage prints Nuk flas gjuha Shqipe. The case is wrong, so that line is not used.

tip: So they know they can keep going.

lesson.background: So they know they can keep going. One word is enough.
facts: Kuptoj is I understand. Nuk kuptoj is I don't.

tip: Polite. Use it when you are not sure.

lesson.background: When you are not sure the sentence landed. Polite you.
facts: A më kuptoni is do you understand me.
Më is me. Kuptoni is understand, polite.

tip: Honest and short.

lesson.background: An honest short answer. Better than guessing.
facts: Nuk e di is I don't know.
E di would be I know it. Nuk flips it.

tip: When the sound will not stick.

lesson.background: When the sound will not stick. A phone note is enough.
facts: A mund is can you, polite.
Ta shkruani is write it.

tip: The everyday order.

lesson.background: The everyday order. Një is one.
facts: They may ask if you want milk before they make it.

tip: Works at a table or in a kitchen.

lesson.background: Works at a table or in a kitchen. They often ask still or sparkling next.
facts: Ujë is water.
Pa gaz is still. Me gaz is sparkling.

tip: Pa gaz means without bubbles.

lesson.background: Still water. Pa gaz means without bubbles.
facts: Say the whole line. Pa gaz is the part that matters.

tip: Me gaz means with bubbles.

lesson.background: Sparkling water. Me gaz means with bubbles.
facts: Gaz here is bubbles, not petrol.

lesson.background: A tea order. They may offer the local herbal tea.
facts: Çaj is tea. Ç is the ch in church.

tip: The local herbal tea.

lesson.background: Mountain tea, the local herbal tea. Often served in a house.
facts: Mali is of the mountain. Çaj mali is the name of the tea.

tip: The usual café coffee.

lesson.background: The usual café coffee. A small strong coffee with a drop of milk.
facts: Makiato is the loanword. You do not need a longer description.

tip: At the end. Some places also say faturën.

lesson.background: At the end, in a café. At home you do not ask for a bill.
facts: Llogarinë is the bill. Some places say faturën.
The number they say changes. The price below is only an example.

tip: Glasses up.

lesson.background: Glasses up, with family or at the table. They usually say it back.
facts: Gëzuar is cheers, literally may it be enjoyed.

tip: Say it to them, polite you.

lesson.background: You say this to them as the food arrives. Polite you.
facts: Ju bëftë mirë is enjoy your meal, said to the people eating.
You will also hear it said to you. That version is in Food, medium.

lesson.background: At a café, before you choose. At home there is often no menu.
facts: Menunë is the menu.
Point if you are not sure they heard.

tip: Point as you say it.

lesson.background: Point at the dish as you say it.
facts: Këtë is this one, the thing you want.
Kjo is this when you are talking about it. Këtë is this when you are asking for it.

lesson.background: When you do not want meat. Say it with the order, not after the plate arrives.
facts: Pa is without. Mish is meat.
It does not name a diet. Add the food if you need to.

tip: A woman says Jam e uritur.

lesson.background: You are telling them you want to eat. They may offer food.
facts: Jam i uritur is I'm hungry, said by a man.
A woman says Jam e uritur.

tip: A woman says Jam e etur.

lesson.background: You want a drink. They often offer water.
facts: Jam i etur is I'm thirsty, said by a man.
A woman says Jam e etur.

lesson.background: A beer order. After it arrives, Gëzuar is the toast.
facts: Birrë is beer.

lesson.background: Cheese. White cheese is common. This line does not name the kind.
facts: Djathë is cheese.
Point, or add the kind, if they have more than one.

lesson.background: A salad. Point at the menu line if there are several.
facts: Sallatë is salad.

lesson.background: Fish. If they name a fish, you can just say Po.
facts: Peshk is fish.
This line does not name which fish.

lesson.background: Chicken. Mish pule is chicken meat.
facts: Pule is hen. Mish is meat.

tip: After you finish.

lesson.background: After you finish, at home or in a café.
facts: Ishte is it was. Shumë e mirë is very good.
At a café, the next line can be the bill. At home, stop at thank you.

tip: When they arrive, or when you arrive to them as a group.

lesson.background: When they arrive, or when you arrive and you are speaking for your group.
facts: Mirë se erdhët is welcome, you have come, polite or plural.
One host talking to one guest may say mirë se erdhe. This line is the ju form.

tip: Point as you say it.

lesson.background: Introduce your son. Point as you say it.
facts: Ky is this, masculine. Djali is the son. Im is my, with a masculine word.
They may ask his name. Say the name after quhet. Ana on other cards is only an example.

lesson.background: Introduce your daughter.
facts: Kjo is this, feminine. Vajza is the daughter. Ime is my, with a feminine word.

lesson.background: Introduce your wife.
facts: Gruaja is the wife. Ime is my, because gruaja is feminine.
Kjo, not ky.

lesson.background: Introduce your husband.
facts: Burri is the husband. Im is my, because burri is masculine.
Ky, not kjo.

tip: When someone is leaving.

lesson.background: When someone is leaving on a trip, not a walk around the block.
facts: Rrugë is road. Të mbarë is may it go well.

tip: The line for the end of a stay.

lesson.background: The line for the end of a stay, after they hosted you.
facts: Mikpritjen is the hospitality.
It is warmer than a plain faleminderit.

albanian: Më ka marrë malli për ju.
phonetic: muh kah MAHR-ruh MAHL-lee pur yoo
tip: Polite you. For one close person people say për ty.

blocks.text: Më ka marrë malli për ju

lesson.background: You missed them. Polite you.
facts: Malli is longing. Më ka marrë malli is I have been missing someone.
For one close person, people say për ty. This line uses për ju.

reply.english: It is good to be with you.
reply.albanian: Është mirë të jem me ju.

tip: Polite you, at bedtime.

lesson.background: At bedtime, to them. Polite you.
facts: Pushoni is rest. Mirë is well.
Natën e mirë is the good-night you already have. This one is the rest.

lesson.background: Your head hurts. Say it to family. Add the doctor line only if you need one.
facts: Më dhemb is it hurts me.
Koka is the head.

answers.english: Do you want us to go to a doctor?
answers.albanian: A doni të shkojmë te mjeku?

lesson.background: Your stomach hurts. Same shape as the head line. Swap the body part.
facts: Barku is the stomach.
Më dhemb stays the same.

tip: A woman says Jam e sëmurë.

lesson.background: You are sick, more than tired.
facts: Jam i sëmurë is I'm sick, said by a man.
A woman says Jam e sëmurë.

answers.english: Do you want us to go to a doctor?
answers.albanian: A doni të shkojmë te mjeku?

lesson.background: You need a doctor. Say where it hurts if you can.
facts: Më duhet is I need.
Mjek is a doctor.

lesson.background: Asking for the pharmacy. They answer with a direction, not a set sentence.
facts: Ku është is where is.
Farmacia is the pharmacy.
Left, right, and straight are their own lines in Getting Around.

tip: Loud and short.

lesson.background: Loud and short, only in an emergency.
facts: Ndihmë is help.
Then say what you need. The ambulance line is the next one if you need it.

tip: Emergency number 127.

lesson.background: Emergency. Say it clearly.
facts: Thirrni is call, polite.
The card tip says 127. Confirm the number where you are. It is not rechecked here.

tip: Then point or name the food.

lesson.background: Say you have an allergy, then name the food or point at it.
facts: Kam is I have. Alergji is an allergy.
This line alone does not say which one.

lesson.background: The word for today. You hear it inside longer lines.
facts: Sot stands on its own.
It does not change for polite you.

lesson.background: The word for tomorrow.
facts: Nesër is tomorrow. Stress the start.

lesson.background: The word for now.
facts: Tani is now. Use it when they offer later and you want this moment.

lesson.background: Later, when now does not work.
facts: Më vonë is later. Vonë alone is late.

lesson.background: What time. They answer with an hour or a part of the day.
facts: Në çfarë ore is at what hour.
Eight below is only an example. The number changes.

tip: Same start as the sit-down line. Swap the verb.

lesson.background: You are offering a meal. Same start as the walk line. The verb is eat.
facts: Hani is eat, polite.
A woman who is hungry says jam e uritur. A man says jam i uritur.

lesson.background: In the morning. A time of day, not a greeting.
facts: Mëngjes is morning. Mirëmëngjes is the greeting, one word.

lesson.background: In the evening.
facts: Mbrëmje is evening. Mirëmbrëma is the greeting.

tip: Same start as Dua të ha. Swap the verb.

lesson.background: I want to drink. Same start as Dua të ha. The verb is pi.
facts: Pi is drink. They may ask what.

answers.english: What do you want to drink?

lesson.background: I want to rest. Same start. The verb is pushoj.
facts: Pushoj is I rest. Pushoni is rest, said to them.

lesson.background: I want to go. Same start. The verb is shkoj.
facts: Shkoj is I go.
They may ask where.

tip: Polite you.

lesson.background: Would you like to drink. Polite you. Same start as the sit line. The verb is pini.
facts: Pini is drink, polite.
The ulni chunk on the sit line is a different story. This drink line is the ordinary polite verb.

tip: Polite you. Mund të ndihmoj is the one you say about yourself.

lesson.background: Can you help me. Polite you. Mund të ndihmoj is the one about yourself.
facts: Më is me. Ndihmoni is help, polite.

tip: In the north you may hear nji.

lesson.background: One. You use it in orders and prices.
facts: In the north you may hear nji. Një is the line to learn.
Një does not change for polite you.

lesson.background: Two.
facts: Dy is two. It stays the same in front of a thing: dy kafe, two coffees.

lesson.background: Three.
facts: Tre is three.

lesson.background: Four.
facts: Katër is four. The ë is a soft uh.

lesson.background: Five.
facts: Pesë is five.

tip: This only plays the count. Each number still has its own box.

lesson.background: Hear them in order. You already met each one alone.

tip: The hundred in the conversation is an example, not a real price.

lesson.background: They ask how many. You say two. The price is an example.
facts: The hundred below is an example. A real price uses whatever number they mean.

lesson.background: Six.
facts: Gjashtë is six.

lesson.background: Seven.
facts: Shtatë is seven.

lesson.background: Eight. You also hear it in times.
facts: Tetë is eight. Në orën tetë is at eight. That hour is only an example.

lesson.background: Nine.
facts: Nëntë is nine.

tip: Dh is the th in this.

lesson.background: Ten.
facts: Dhjetë is ten. Dh is the th in this.

lesson.background: Twenty. Useful in prices.
facts: Njëzet is twenty. It is one word.

lesson.background: Fifty.
facts: Pesëdhjetë is fifty, five and ten stuck together.

lesson.background: One hundred. Common in small prices.
facts: Njëqind is one hundred, one word.
A price like njëqind lekë is an example. The number changes.

tip: Old prices in lek can sound bigger than they are. Ask if you are unsure.

lesson.background: One thousand.
facts: Një mijë is one thousand, two words.
Old prices in lek can sound bigger than they are. Ask if you are unsure.

tip: The money question after the price.

lesson.background: The money question after you hear a price, or when you want it in lek.
facts: Sa is how many. Lekë is lek, the money.
The answers below are examples. A real price uses whatever number they mean.

tip: At a market stall.

lesson.background: At a market stall, when the price is too high. You can walk away.
facts: E shtrenjtë is expensive, feminine, matching the thing or the price.
Shumë makes it too, or very.

lesson.background: Where is the toilet. They answer with a direction.
facts: Ku është is where is. Tualeti is the toilet.
Wikivoyage prints this sentence. The pronunciation in its parentheses does not match these words, so it is not shown.
Here, over there, left, and right are the words you will hear. They are not one fixed sentence.

lesson.background: Where is the bus station.
facts: Stacioni i autobusit is the bus station.
After they point, you can ask if it is far.

lesson.background: Is it far. Ask after they point.
facts: Larg is far. Afër is close.

lesson.background: Is it close.
facts: Afër is close. The opposite of larg.

lesson.background: Left. You say it to a driver, or you hear it when you ask the way.
facts: Majtas is left.
It can stand alone.

lesson.background: Right.
facts: Djathtas is right.

lesson.background: Straight ahead.
facts: Drejt is straight. Përpara is ahead.

tip: Taxi or minibus.

lesson.background: Stop here. Taxi or minibus.
facts: Ndaloni is stop, polite.
Këtu is here.

lesson.background: A ticket. Say where if they ask.
facts: Biletë is a ticket.
They may ask where, or how many.

lesson.background: You want a taxi. Say the place name after, if you know it.
facts: Taksi is taxi.
This line does not name the place.

answers.english: Where do you want to go?

lesson.background: You are lost. Then ask for the place.
facts: Kam humbur is I am lost, I have gotten lost.

answers.english: Where do you want to go?

tip: The shared van between towns.

lesson.background: The shared van between towns. You can say the word to ask for it.
facts: Furgon is the van. Furgoni is the van, as the subject.
It is not the city bus.

tip: Point at the thing.

lesson.background: How much is this. Point at the thing.
facts: Sa kushton is how much does it cost.
Kjo is this.
The prices below are examples. The number changes.

tip: Outside towns, often no.

lesson.background: Do you take cards. Outside towns, often no.
facts: Pranoni is you accept, polite.
Kartë is card.

lesson.background: I'll take it. After you hear the price and you want it.
facts: Do ta marr is I will take it.

lesson.background: I'm just looking. When they ask if they can help.
facts: Vetëm is only. Po shoh is I am looking.

lesson.background: You don't want it. Short, and enough.
facts: Nuk e dua is I don't want it.

tip: Point.

lesson.background: Do you have this. Point.
facts: A keni is do you have, polite.
Këtë is this one.

lesson.background: A bag, if they do not hand you one.
facts: Qese is a bag.

tip: Size. Not checked against every shop habit.

lesson.background: Smaller, please. Size. The wording is not checked against every shop habit.
facts: Më të vogël is smaller.
If they do not have a size, you will hear that they don't have it.

tip: At the door.

lesson.background: At the door. You are letting them in.
facts: Hyni is come in, polite.
Then they usually thank you.

lesson.background: Where can we sleep. Ask the host, not a stranger.
facts: Ku mund të flejmë is where can we sleep.
Flejmë is we sleep.

lesson.background: Sorry we are late, when you arrive after you said.
facts: Na falni is excuse us.
U vonuam is we were late.

lesson.background: The keys. When you are leaving the house, or picking them up.
facts: Çelësat is the keys.

lesson.background: Where is the kitchen. In a house you are staying in.
facts: Kuzhina is the kitchen.
Ku është is where is.

english: Can I help in the kitchen?
albanian: A mund të ndihmoj në kuzhinë?
phonetic: ah moond tuh ndeeh-MOY nuh koo-ZHEE-nuh

lesson.background: Can I help in the kitchen. A good offer after a meal.
facts: Në kuzhinë is in the kitchen.
Mund të ndihmoj is can I help.

tip: The house, the view, the food.

lesson.background: The house, the view, the food. A warm comment, not a question.
facts: Bukur is beautiful. Shumë makes it very.
Është is it is.

tip: Two lines you already know, said together.

lesson.background: Two lines you already know, said together at bedtime.
facts: Natën e mirë is good night.
Pushoni mirë is rest well.

tip: What you may hear after you ask how they are.

lesson.background: This is their answer. You asked how they are.
facts: Po ju? sends the question back to you, politely.

tip: A short answer to how are you.

lesson.background: They may say only this, with no question back.
facts: Jam is I am. Mirë is well.

tip: A man says i lodhur. A woman says e lodhur.

lesson.background: An honest answer when the day was long.
facts: A woman says Pak e lodhur.

tip: Shorter than a full goodbye.

lesson.background: They expect to see you again. Not a final goodbye.
facts: Shihemi means we will see each other.

tip: After you asked and you.

lesson.background: They answer your Po ju?
facts: Edhe means also. Unë is I.

tip: Ana is only an example.

lesson.background: You asked their name. The real name replaces Ana.
facts: The name sits right after quhem.

tip: When they say they are pleased to meet you.

lesson.background: Their answer to Më vjen mirë.
facts: Edhe mua means me too.

tip: They accepted a yes or a no.

lesson.background: You will hear this when something is settled.
facts: It means all right, or that's fine.

tip: The whole hello, not one word on its own.

lesson.background: Morning at the door. You walk in. You greet, they ask how you are, you answer, you ask back.
facts: Start with Mirëmëngjes. Wait. Then answer.

tip: Thank them, then say goodbye.

lesson.background: Leaving the house. You are at the door. Thank them, then leave the door open for another meeting.
facts: Mirupafshim is the full goodbye. Shihemi means you will see them again.

tip: You hear this after you ask them to slow down.

lesson.background: They agreed to slow down.
facts: Po is yes.
Flas is I speak. Ngadalë is slowly.

tip: A warm reaction when you try a line.

lesson.background: You will hear this when a sentence lands.
facts: Shumë is very. Mirë is good.

tip: Their answer when they speak some English, or you speak some Albanian.

lesson.background: Short for a little. The rest of the sentence is understood.
facts: Pak is a little.

tip: You stop them, they slow down, you thank them.

lesson.background: Too fast. They were fast. You ask, they agree, you close it.
facts: The first line is the one you say.
Wait for them to answer before thank you.

tip: At a table, a shop, or a door. Here you are, or please go on.

lesson.background: You hear this when they hand you something, or invite you to speak.
facts: Urdhëroni is polite you. One person your age may hear urdhëro.

tip: They need a minute. Wait.

lesson.background: After you order. Not a no.
facts: Një is one. Moment is a moment.

tip: They are checking the coffee.

lesson.background: A question. Answer yes or say the order again.
facts: Me is with. Qumësht is milk.

tip: They are checking the water.

lesson.background: Pa gaz is still water. Me gaz is sparkling.
facts: Answer with the water line you want.

tip: You order, they ask about milk, you answer.

lesson.background: Ordering a coffee. The whole order, not the first word only.
facts: Wait for the milk question.
Then answer with milk, or say the still-water shape if you changed your mind.

tip: You hear this as the plate arrives. The beginner line is you saying it to them.

lesson.background: Said to you, polite.
facts: Ju is you. Bëftë mirë is may it do you good.

tip: They are still offering. You can say no.

lesson.background: Polite you. At home, one person may say ha edhe pak instead.
facts: Hani is eat. Edhe pak is a little more.

tip: An invitation to start.

lesson.background: You hear this when the food is ready.
facts: Hani is eat, polite.

tip: You are full. They offer more. You say no.

lesson.background: They keep offering. A full plate and a second offer.
facts: Ngopur is full. Some speakers add i or e before it.

tip: Their answer to we love you.

lesson.background: Edhe ne is us too. Ju duam is we love you, polite.
facts: You do not need a long answer.

tip: Short for us too, after you say you missed them or you are glad.

lesson.background: Edhe is also. Ne is we.
facts: Edhe mua is me too, from one person.

tip: You hear this when you walk in. The beginner card is you saying it.

lesson.background: Said to you, or to your group.
facts: Mirë se erdhët is you have come well.

tip: You thank them for everything. They brush it off. You say you love them.

lesson.background: End of the visit. At the door, when the stay is over.
facts: Për gjithçka is for everything.

english: Do you want us to go to a doctor?
albanian: A doni të shkojmë te mjeku?
phonetic: ah DOH-nee tuh SHKOY-muh teh MYEH-koo
tip: They are offering to take you.

lesson.background: A yes-or-no question. A is the question mark in the words.
facts: Te mjeku is at the doctor.

tip: You hear this when you say something hurts.

lesson.background: The same sorry you already learned to say. Here someone says it to you.
facts: You can thank them, or say what you need.

tip: A short question. They want a place or a body part.

lesson.background: Ku is where. One word.
facts: Answer with the place, or point.

tip: You say it, they are sorry, you ask for a pharmacy.

lesson.background: Not an ambulance. A head, then a pharmacy.
facts: If it is an emergency, use the help line instead.

tip: An example hour. The number changes.

lesson.background: You hear this after what time.
facts: Në orën is at the hour. Tetë is eight.
Swap the number. This eight is only an example.

tip: They are saying today does not work.

lesson.background: Sot is today. Jo is no. Today, no.
facts: You can move it to tomorrow.

tip: They accepted the walk or the outing.

lesson.background: Po is yes. Shkojmë is let's go, we go.
facts: Then you can set the time.

english: Do you want to take a walk?
tip: You invite them. They say yes. You set the morning.

lesson.background: A walk. One invitation, carried through.
facts: Shëtisim is we stroll.

english: What do you want to drink?
tip: They ask this after you say you want to drink.

lesson.background: Çfarë is what. Doni is you want, polite. Të pini is to drink.
facts: Answer with the drink.

tip: A strong yes, when you asked for help.

lesson.background: Sigurisht is of course, surely.
facts: You can thank them.

tip: They are telling you to rest.

lesson.background: Pushoni is rest, polite you.
facts: Po agrees with what you said.

tip: You offer. They accept. You close it.

lesson.background: Offering help. Help, accepted.
facts: Mund të ndihmoj is can I help.

tip: The short question behind prices and counts.

lesson.background: Sa is how much or how many. One word.
facts: Answer with a number.

tip: An example price. The number changes.

lesson.background: You hear a number, then lekë.
facts: Njëqind is one hundred.
This hundred is an example, not a real price.

tip: Another example price.

lesson.background: Pesëdhjetë is fifty.
facts: Example only.

tip: You ask. They say a number. You take it or you don't.

lesson.background: Asking the price in lek. One price, then your answer.
facts: The hundred is an example.

tip: A direction. Look where they point.

lesson.background: Atje is over there, not in your hand.
facts: Këtu is here.

tip: Close by. They may point at a door.

lesson.background: Këtu is here.
facts: It can be a room, a chair, or a stop.

tip: The answer to is it far, when it is not.

lesson.background: Afër is close.
facts: Larg is far.

english: Where do you want to go?
tip: A driver, or someone helping you when you are lost.

lesson.background: Doni is you want, polite. Të shkoni is to go.
facts: Say the place if you know it. This course does not name one.

tip: You ask. They point left. You thank them.

lesson.background: Asking the way. A place, a direction, a thank you.
facts: Atje, majtas is over there, on the left. Other places get other directions.

tip: They do not take a card.

lesson.background: Jo is no. Vetëm lekë is only lek.
facts: Some people say cash. This line says lek.

tip: The short no. They are out of it.

lesson.background: S'kemi is we don't have. The full form is nuk kemi.
facts: You can thank them and look elsewhere.

tip: They are handing you the thing.

lesson.background: Ja is here, as they pass it to you.
facts: One syllable.

tip: A shopkeeper inviting you in, or to say what you want.

lesson.background: Same word as at the café.
facts: Then you can ask the price.

tip: You ask the price. They say a number. You take it.

lesson.background: At the stall. Point, ask, hear a price, decide.
facts: One hundred lek is an example, not a quote.
This is the price question. A shorter recording, Sa është, is its own card.

tip: Keys, or a towel, put in your hand.

lesson.background: Same short word as in a shop.
facts: You thank them.

tip: You hear this after sorry we are late.

lesson.background: S'ka problem is there's no problem.
facts: You can thank them and go in.

tip: The room, the kitchen, the bed. They point.

lesson.background: Këtu is here, inside the house as well as on the street.
facts: Look where they point.

tip: You apologize. They say it is fine. You thank them.

lesson.background: Arriving late. Late to the door.
facts: Na falni is excuse us. U vonuam is we were late.

facts: The wording is the book's, including its spelling.
